comment: The decisive miss was E<A<B: B’s shallow, wider architecture did not compensate for its reduced nonlinear composition. Residual paths and terminal normalization plausibly let E and A learn interactions faster, but gold alone does not isolate that mechanism. I overextended K1033’s 32-epoch, 2-versus-4-block reversal to this 16-epoch, 1–3-block comparison. K1009’s shallow preference was likewise too broad; K1056 helped select D but is only tentative at Δ=.0768. Backtesting normalized residual-depth comparisons at Δ=.03–.1 found deeper wins in only 2/4 historical pairs and 4/6 lab pairs; the sole sparse-interaction lab pair favored shallower. Thus neither universal shallow preference nor its reversal is supported, and I propose no new rule.
